name: Math Mammoth
line: Math Mammoth is a book the adult places, checks and reviews. AMP does all three, one answer at a time.
description: AMP vs Math Mammoth: a $245.50 set of K-8 worktexts the adult checks by hand, or practice that explains every answer and schedules review. Prices and evidence.
verdict: Math Mammoth is a visual set of worktexts that Maria Miller has written and sold since 2003. The full K-8 download costs $245.50, paid once [4][7]. The book is the same for every child, and the adult places the child, checks the work, finds the gaps and decides when to review [3][11][12]. AMP does those jobs itself at every answer, and it keeps going through precalculus.

reasons.title: A wrong answer is explained on the spot
reasons.body: In Math Mammoth a child works the exercises on paper. Then the child or the adult checks them against the answer key, and the adult decides what to do about a mistake [11]. AMP marks each answer as it is given and shows the correct answer with worked steps, and a one-step hint and a written lesson wait beside every problem. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, feedback that explains averaged an effect of 0.49, and marking right or wrong alone averaged 0.05 [16].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math, kept current
reasons.body: Math Mammoth places a child with a free end-of-year test for each grade: 80 to 89% means start the next grade, below 50% means try a lower test [12]. From there the child follows the book's fixed order, and the adult decides what to add [11]. AMP places the learner within the first 24 problems and keeps a level in each of 14 strands and keeps adjusting with every answer. A child strong in geometry and still building fractions works at both levels in the same session.

reasons.title: Misses lead back to the skill underneath
reasons.body: Math Mammoth fills gaps with its Blue Series, topic books the adult chooses and puts in order [3]. Its chapters end in a test, with no numeric rule for mastery that we could find [11]. In AMP, two misses in a row on a skill send practice to what that skill builds on. A skill counts as Strong at four of the last five answers right without help, after at least five tries.

reasons.title: Old skills return on a fixed schedule
reasons.body: Math Mammoth ends each chapter with a mixed review lesson, includes cumulative review sheets, and sells spiral Skills Review workbooks separately [2][11]. When to use them is the adult's call [11]. AMP brings every learned skill back after 6 hours, 1 day, 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks and a month, mixed with other topics. A miss starts the schedule over.

reasons.title: It keeps going past grade 8
reasons.body: Math Mammoth's complete-curriculum page says it does not offer algebra 1 or above [2]. AMP runs from counting through Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 and Precalculus on one map of 336 skills. A learner who uses AMP beside the worktexts keeps the same program and the same record after grade 8.

reasons.title: Paper printed for one learner
reasons.body: Math Mammoth's books are the same for every child, and its worksheet maker adds practice on topics the adult picks [2]. AMP prints unlimited workbooks built from the learner's own record, with that day's review and a worked answer key. Results entered from paper count toward the learner's level. A family that loves Math Mammoth's lessons can keep them and use AMP for practice and review.

rows.price: Downloads, paid once: K-8 bundle $245.50, K-4 $133, grades 5-8 $112.50 [4]. Printed copies sold by outside stores [8].
rows.buyers: Families, from the author's site; one license per teacher [5]. Schools by quote [6]. For ESA funds, the author points to resellers on state lists [5].
rows.range: Light Blue Series: kindergarten through grade 8. No algebra 1 or above [2].
rows.start: Free end-of-year placement tests for each grade, with percent cutoffs and section scores to spot gaps [12].
rows.teaching: Worktext lessons written to the student, with worked examples and visual models [2][7]. Free videos for many lessons [9][11].
rows.next: The next lesson in the book. The adult decides what to add, skip or review [11].
rows.mastery: Mastery-based chapters, each ending in a test. No numeric mastery rule stated [11].
rows.review: A mixed review lesson per chapter, cumulative review sheets, and spiral review workbooks sold separately. The adult times them [2][11].
rows.print: PDF books to print at home, with full answer keys and tests [2]. The same book for every child.
rows.adult: Plan the schedule, check answers with the key, give chapter tests, and choose when to add review or games. No scripted lessons [11].
rows.reports: None found. The adult grades by hand with the answer key; rubrics are optional [11].
rows.evidence: No rating from Evidence for ESSA [14]. No What Works Clearinghouse intervention report [15]. No outcome study found on its site [1][13].

theirs: Math Mammoth is a series of math worktexts by Maria Miller, sold from MathMammoth.com since 2003 [7]. Miller holds a master's degree in mathematics and began writing after tutoring homeschoolers [7]. The complete curriculum, the Light Blue Series, runs from kindergarten through grade 8 [2]. The Blue Series holds the same lessons sorted by topic, for filling gaps or building a custom course [3].

A lesson is a few pages written to the student: an explanation, worked examples and visual models, then exercises on paper [2][7]. The author suggests watching a child for a week or two to find a workable pace, and gives a pages-per-week guide for each grade [11]. The adult plans the schedule, checks the work with the answer key and gives the chapter tests [11].

The books are PDF downloads. Families print them or buy printed copies from outside stores such as Lulu and Rainbow Resource [8]. Free extras include placement tests, videos for many lessons and online practice games [9][10][12].
credit: A much lower price. The K-8 download bundle is $245.50, paid once [4]. AMP costs $599 a year for the first child.
Lessons a child can read alone. The author writes that students can often read and study the lessons on their own [11].
Paper first, and fully offline once downloaded, apart from the worksheet maker [2]. AMP runs in a browser and needs a connection.
Free tools before you buy: placement tests with clear cutoffs, videos for many lessons, and online games for math facts [9][10][12]. AMP has no games.
Editions beyond the U.S. one: Spanish on a separate site, plus International, Canadian and South African versions [1]. AMP is in English only.

theirs: We found no outcome study of Math Mammoth on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in the What Works Clearinghouse as of November 2026. Evidence for ESSA lists Math Mammoth without a rating ("No studies met inclusion requirements") [14]. The What Works Clearinghouse has no intervention report on it [15]. The home page cites no research [1].

Its own testimonials page carries parent and teacher stories, several with one child's test scores [13]. None that we read has a comparison group. Miller's visual models do have general support: the What Works Clearinghouse's 2021 guide for elementary students who struggle in math rates concrete and semi-concrete representations as strong evidence [19]. That backs the method in general. It is not a study of Math Mammoth.
ours: A mastery book teaches one topic at a time and leaves the timing of review to the adult. AMP schedules it, and spacing is among the best-supported methods in learning research. A review of ten study techniques rated two as high utility, spaced practice and practice testing [18]. In a randomized trial of 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed, spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [17]. We expect that to show in outcomes, and we have committed to measuring it in public.

AMP is new, and its own outcome studies have not run yet. They begin in 2027: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. Until then, the research behind each part of AMP is laid out in our report, and the code is public.

them: Choose Math Mammoth if price comes first: one payment covers the K-8 books for your family.
Choose Math Mammoth if you want math on paper and off the internet.
Choose Math Mammoth if your child learns well from reading a book and you are glad to check the work.
Choose Math Mammoth if you need a Spanish, Canadian or South African edition.
amp: You want every answer checked and explained the moment it is given, without an answer key.
You want the level found in each part of math, and practice that follows the learner.
You want review to come back on its own schedule, without planning it.
Your learner is ready for algebra, geometry or beyond.
You love Math Mammoth's lessons and want checking, review and personal workbooks beside them.

questions.question: Is Math Mammoth cheaper than AMP?
questions.answer: Yes. The K-8 download bundle is $245.50, paid once [4]. AMP is $599 a year or $59 a month for the first child, and $399 or $39 for each more. That buys placement in every strand, a check and worked steps on every answer, scheduled review, unlimited personal workbooks and a range through precalculus.

questions.question: Can we use AMP alongside Math Mammoth?
questions.answer: Yes. Keep the worktexts for lessons and use AMP for practice, checking and review. AMP keeps its own order, but a parent can point practice at any skill on its map.

questions.question: What comes after Math Mammoth?
questions.answer: Math Mammoth does not offer algebra 1 or above [2]. AMP continues through Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 and Precalculus, and places the learner within the first 24 problems, with a level in each strand.

questions.question: Is Math Mammoth self-teaching?
questions.answer: The author calls it "nearly self-teaching" for many children [2]. The adult still plans the schedule, checks answers with the key, gives the tests and decides when to review [11].
